title: Dockerized runner for reproducible benchmarking (pinned deps + deterministic env capture)
author: Rina Kobayashi
description:
Motivation: We’ve been seeing small but persistent drift between benchmark sweeps run from different runner hosts (package resolver differences, CUDA/PyTorch mismatches, minor lib updates). For the public benchmark report we need deterministic reruns (or at minimum: a fully captured environment we can replay) when data validation or Legal asks for substantiation. This PR introduces a Dockerized benchmark runner image with pinned dependencies and a small amount of metadata plumbing so each run manifest records the exact container digest + runtime versions used.

What’s in this PR: Adds a GPU-capable Docker image for benchmark-lab runners based on NVIDIA CUDA runtime, with pinned Python + pip deps, and a reproducible build process (no floating tags). Adds `requirements.lock.txt` (generated from `requirements.in`) and a build arg for CUDA minor version to support our current fleet (12.1/12.2). Adds `bench env` command to dump versions (Python, torch, transformers, CUDA, driver, kernel) and writes them into the run manifest automatically. Adds documentation in README: how to build locally, how to run on a GPU host, and how to run region sweeps via the same container.

Non-goals: This does not change benchmark logic/metrics. It does not attempt bit-for-bit determinism of kernels across driver versions; it’s about making the environment explicit and reproducible enough that reruns are comparable and explainable.

Implementation notes: Uses multi-stage build to keep image size reasonable; wheels are installed from pinned hashes where available. The runner defaults to non-root user and only mounts a working directory (no implicit access to host credentials). Adds a smoke-test GitHub Action that builds the image and runs `bench --help` plus a tiny CPU-only unit test shard to ensure packaging stays healthy.

Checklist: - [x] Image builds in CI and locally - [x] Runner prints captured env info - [x] Run manifest includes container digest + dependency versions - [x] README updated with usage + troubleshooting - [x] Confirmed no secrets/baked-in tokens - [x] Confirmed license headers for base image are referenced in NOTICE

Rollout: Once merged, Infra will update the region sweep runners to use `ghcr.io/redwoodinference/benchmark-lab-runner:<git_sha>` and pin by digest in the scheduler config. We can keep existing bare-metal instructions for now but should prefer Docker for all report-bound runs.

illustrative_snippet:
Example: running a sweep via Docker

  docker run --rm --gpus all \
    -v "$PWD:/work" -w /work \
    ghcr.io/redwoodinference/benchmark-lab-runner@sha256:<digest> \
    bench run --config configs/prod_mix_v3.yaml --out artifacts/run.json

Manifest now includes:
  container_image: ghcr.io/redwoodinference/benchmark-lab-runner
  container_digest: sha256:…
  env: { python: 3.11.8, torch: 2.3.1+cu121, transformers: 4.44.2, cuda_runtime: 12.1, driver: 550.54.15, … }
review_conversation:
Claire Dubois (review): Can we guarantee the lock file is actually used in the image build (vs pip resolving at build time)? Also please clarify in README that driver versions can still impact p95.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Yep — Docker build now copies `requirements.lock.txt` and installs with `--require-hashes` where hashes are present; otherwise it pins exact versions. Added README note about driver/kernel impact and that we record driver version in the manifest.

Jonas Weber (review): Image size looks high in the build logs (~9.8GB). Can we drop dev tooling (gcc, git) from final stage? Also please add a way to print the container digest from inside the runner.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Switched to multi-stage: build wheels in builder stage, runtime stage only has Python venv + shared libs. Size down to ~4.1GB compressed in GHCR. Added `bench env` output includes `RUNNER_IMAGE_DIGEST` when present (CI injects label + env).

Omar El-Sayed (review): Any risk we bake in AWS creds via build context? Please ensure `.dockerignore` excludes local config and artifacts.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Added `.dockerignore` patterns for `.aws`, `.gcp`, `artifacts/`, `datasets/`, and common dotenv files. Build action runs in clean workspace.

Neha Kapoor (review): For fleet runners, we need a stable tag policy. Can we publish SHA tags and recommend pinning by digest in production configs?

Rina Kobayashi (author): Updated README + added note in description: publish `:<git_sha>` but recommend digest pinning for report runs. Infra can still use floating tags for dev.

Jonas Weber (follow-up): One more: can we ensure the container runs as non-root and doesn’t write outside /work?

Rina Kobayashi (author): Final stage uses `USER bench` with UID/GID set; default workdir is `/work`. Added a quick smoke test to verify uid != 0.

Result: Approved by Claire/Jonas/Omar/Neha. Squash merged.
